evals.prompt: Optimize the CLAUDE.md of the project in evals/files/bloated/. It has grown a lot and I think Claude ignores half of it now.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten evals/files/bloated/CLAUDE.md, well under its original 78 lines, that keeps the non-guessable commands and gotchas, replaces the API endpoint dump with a prose pointer to docs/api.md, resolves the test-suite contradiction, drops the self-evident advice and the derivable dependency list, and reports the before and after counts.
expectations: The output CLAUDE.md has fewer than 40 lines
The output CLAUDE.md still contains the single-test command `npm test -- <path>` or an equivalent that names the path argument
The output CLAUDE.md still says that `src/generated/` must not be edited by hand
The output CLAUDE.md still says the API tests need a local Redis
The output CLAUDE.md does not list the endpoints POST /v1/users, GET /v1/users/:id, or PATCH /v1/users/:id
The output CLAUDE.md points to docs/api.md without a bare `@docs/api.md` import (the path is in backticks or plain prose, or the line is gone)
The output CLAUDE.md does not import docs/release.md with `@docs/release.md`
The output CLAUDE.md contains exactly one rule about running the test suite, and it does not both require the full suite on every commit and forbid it
The output CLAUDE.md does not contain the phrases 'write clean code', 'meaningful variable names', or 'follow best practices'
The output CLAUDE.md does not list the dependencies express, pg, or zod
Every file path mentioned in the output CLAUDE.md exists in the fixture project
The response reports the before and after line counts
The response shows the classification or the diff before the file is written, or states that it is writing after showing it
The kept lines about Redis, `src/generated/`, `DATABASE_URL`, 2-space indentation, and ES modules appear with their original wording (at least 4 of the 5 verbatim), not rephrased
The lint rule is not silently weakened: either it stays as 'after editing any file' or it becomes a hook; it is not rewritten as 'before committing' without a hook
The response reports character counts alongside line counts

evals.prompt: hey, evals/files/bloated/CLAUDE.md is huge, can you slim it down? the release steps should probably live somewhere else, and I want the lint rule to actually run every time, Claude keeps forgetting it
evals.expected_output: The same trim as eval 1, plus the Releasing section moved out to a skill (or a pointer to docs/release.md) and the ALWAYS-run-lint rule turned into a PostToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json with the CLAUDE.md line removed.
expectations: The output CLAUDE.md no longer contains the numbered release steps
The release procedure is reachable: either a skill under .claude/skills/ was created or the output CLAUDE.md points to docs/release.md as a prose pointer
A PostToolUse hook matching Edit or Write that runs the lint command exists in .claude/settings.json
The output CLAUDE.md no longer contains the 'ALWAYS run npm run lint:fix' line
The output CLAUDE.md contains no line written in all-caps emphasis such as IMPORTANT or NEVER
The output CLAUDE.md has fewer than 40 lines
The kept lines about Redis, `src/generated/`, and `DATABASE_URL` appear with their original wording, not rephrased
The response shows the block-by-block classification or the diff before stating that the files were written

evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/lean/CLAUDE.md and tell me what you would change.
evals.expected_output: Little or nothing. The file is already short and every line is load-bearing. The skill should recognize that, keep the odd-looking but non-obvious gotchas, not invent docs to point to, and not rewrite the surviving lines.
expectations: The rule 'make test-one T=<name>' is kept
The rule about `build/config.yaml` being regenerated by `make gen` is kept
The rule about the 32-bit target is kept
The response does not propose pointing to a docs/ directory, CONTRIBUTING.md, or any file that does not exist in the fixture
If a rewritten CLAUDE.md is produced, at most 2 of its lines differ in wording from the original
The response reports the before and after line counts, or states that no change is needed
The response explains, for each kept rule, why it passes the keep test (a per-block verdict, not a blanket 'looks fine')
